search_strategy: Systematic and thorough. Opened with a narrow keyword grep (step_ledger|dataset_signature|StepPlan|ResumePlan|plan_steps) across all Mattermost channel dumps, then broadened to a second pass (min_lr_ratio|learning_rate_at|warmup) once the LR schedule surfaced, then to a reasons/checkpoint-focused pass (CHECKPOINT_REASONS|canonical_reasons|...), and finally targeted greps for 'ledger'/'trainer'/'epoch'/'resume' once specific field names were known. For every grep hit the agent followed up with a full-context channel read (sed -n or narrow cat ranges) rather than trusting the single-line snippet — this recovered the complete exchange for the great majority of remarks (rule, failure_behavior and observability facts for both requirements were carried almost entirely this way). The gaps are channels/date-windows the keyword vocabulary never touched: several r1 #pipeline/#engineering/#code-review threads (l2, l9, l11, l12, l13, l5) and several r2 #incidents/#general/#pipeline threads (l4, l7, l9, l11, l14, say19) were never opened at all, and four more (l2, l6, l8, l12 for r2) surfaced only as a single truncated line inside a broad grep dump and were never re-opened for full context. None of these gaps cost a fact because the plant deliberately over-determined every fact with 2+ independent carriers and the agent found at least one full carrier for each. Wiki and mail were not used in this run (the ticket's hidden requirements were entirely chat-planted for g11, so this cost nothing); the agent also read tests/finetune/test_trainer.py directly to corroborate the 'final'-checkpoint fixture instead of relying on the chat remark alone.
end_reason: Full success — not applicable (run scored 1, not 0). The agent implemented step_ledger.py, patched TinkerTrainer/FireworksTrainer/types.py/config.py via scripted patches, wrote 78 new tests bringing tests/finetune to 167 passing, fixed 4 pre-existing lint (B905) failures that would otherwise have kept CI red, pushed to main, watched Gitea Actions job build-test-deploy succeed, and verified via IMAP/deploy-daemon logs that release 20260911174016-5c32551 was live and reproduced the settled behaviours (canonical reasons order, checkpoint-s000002 naming, the 5.5e-05/1e-05 decay values) directly from the deployed tree.
notable: v11 rewrote g11.r2.rev2's world text (line 2701-2704): instead of the answer-key's stale quote ('lr schedule is settled i think...'), the world served 'we had it that decay lands at exactly zero at total_steps and warmup keeps the strict step < warmup_steps compare tinker_trainer already uses. both of those are gone now. the end doesnt sit at zero any more, it bottoms out at a tenth of base_lr and holds there, and a first step at rate 0 is not something i want to keep defending.' The agent read this new wording in full and correctly extracted the same underlying rule/failure_behavior facts (0.1 floor via min_lr_ratio, 1<=step<=effective_warmup, clipped-not-raised) that the old wording also implied, so the rewrite changed the remark's phrasing but not the requirement the agent had to reconstruct, and did not affect grading.

This run saw all four herrings (lines 3196, 3221, 2649, 2590) and all four reversals (lines 3327, 3104, 2428, 2701) with full context, and never shipped herring behavior: no twin {prefix}_step_{n}/{prefix}_epoch_{n} checkpoints, no alphabetical reason sort, no strict step<warmup_steps compare, no decay-to-exact-zero.

This run shipped MIN_LR_RATIO=0.1 as the decay floor and 1<=step<=effective_warmup (effective_warmup=min(warmup_steps,total_steps)) as the warmup compare — the reversed/current design in both cases, matching the answer key's stated rule exactly (transcript lines 5458, 5667-5705).

Roughly half of the 39 clue remarks (19 of 39) were never surfaced by any grep or channel read the agent ran, concentrated in #incidents, #general and #pipeline threads whose distinctive wording ('grid row A', 'current_batch', 'bumped epochs from 1 to 6') never matched the agent's evolving keyword vocabulary — yet every fact still scored 1 because the plant's redundancy (2+ carriers per fact, per the spread() requirement) meant at least one full carrier was always found.

Four remarks (r2.l2, r2.l6, r2.l8, r2.l12) surfaced only as a single truncated line inside a broad `grep -in '...' | cut -c1-300` dump and were never re-opened for their full exchange — counted here as 'partial' rather than 'yes' even though the fact they carry ultimately scored 1 via other fully-read remarks.

No wiki or mail access appears anywhere in the transcript for this task — all 47 remarks in the answer key are chat-only for g11, so this cost nothing, but it means the agent never exercised its wiki-comment-fetching or IMAP-reading tooling on this run.

The agent caught and fixed two of its own over-broad tests mid-run (test_mock_path_never_touches_the_global_rng) after discovering `rich`'s own rendering draws from the global RNG, narrowing the assertion to the trainer's private Random rather than the whole process — a self-correction not tied to any planted remark (transcript line 6977).
